decisionChange: Visual quality, aesthetic coherence and authoring throughput are now primary criteria while browser-link delivery remains a hard requirement.
hardRequirements: Static-hostable browser build with WebGL2 fallback and no player installation
A coherent stylized art direction with controlled lighting, materials, color and post-processing
glTF-centered replaceable asset pipeline with stable asset IDs and provenance
Animation, camera and environment iteration that does not entangle authoritative gameplay state
Deterministic and serializable identity/fact/witness rules testable without rendering
Quality presets and measured frame, memory, draw-call, texture and download budgets

visualQualityModel.principle: Judge a repeatable authored target frame at playable performance, not feature count or a single offline-looking screenshot.
targetFrameIngredients: Salt-whitened stone and oxidized bronze material family
Late-afternoon directional light with readable threshold shadows
Sea haze and restrained atmospheric depth
Character silhouettes readable against port architecture
A controlled warm-stone / cold-sea palette with one rumor accent
Filmic tone mapping and restrained bloom without destroying UI or evidence legibility
antiGoals: Effect-heavy image with unreadable interaction thresholds
WebGPU-only showcase that fails the baseline browser route
Visual polish embedded directly in game-state code

evaluationModel.rule: weightedTotal = sum(score * weight); differences below 2 points require a decision-driving visual bake-off or explicit human risk acceptance

candidates.label: Babylon.js + TypeScript + Blender/glTF
qualityCase: Integrated PBR, HDR/EXR image-based lighting, soft and cascaded shadows, volumetric lighting, post-processing, reflection probes and screen-space effects reduce bespoke renderer assembly.
Node Material, Node Render Graph, particle and GUI editors plus Inspector improve look-development iteration.
glTF import/export and animation retargeting fit a Blender-centered authored asset pipeline.
constraints: Use stable PBRMaterial for the first slice; do not make newer OpenPBR behavior a release dependency without a focused compatibility check.
Keep WebGL2 as the baseline and treat WebGPU as progressive enhancement.
The deterministic domain model remains plain TypeScript and cannot depend on Babylon scene nodes.

candidates.label: Three.js + React Three Fiber + TypeScript + Blender/glTF
qualityCase: Very high shader, node-material, tone-mapping, color-grading and post-processing control.
React/DOM information design and deterministic TypeScript state integration are already proven in the spike.
The WebGPU renderer offers a modern node-based post-processing path while WebGL2 can remain the baseline.
constraints: Scene inspection, animation authoring, navigation and material tooling require more custom assembly.
The current spike already triggers a large-chunk warning before real assets are added.
High artistic ceiling is irrelevant if bespoke tools consume the demo schedule.

candidates.label: Godot 4 GDScript Compatibility Web + Blender/glTF
qualityCase: Best integrated scene, animation, material and camera authoring workflow of the three candidates.
Strong glTF/Blender import and live scene inspection.
constraints: Browser export uses the least advanced Compatibility renderer rather than Forward+.
Compatibility rendering does not provide some high-end effects such as SDFGI and volumetric fog/fog volumes.
WASM/PCK delivery and browser threading constraints weaken the link-first objective.

provisionalRecommendation.oneSentence: Babylon.js now ranks first because its integrated rendering and authoring tools are more likely to convert art direction into a polished browser scene without spending the demo budget on custom engine tooling.
provisionalRecommendation.notEnoughToLock: The 1.25-point lead is below the two-point evidence threshold and no comparable target-frame browser evidence exists.

sameInputs: One procedural salt-stone gate, bronze seal, cloth banner and water plane
One fixed oblique camera and one close character-reading camera
One fixed HDR-like lighting intent and shared palette values
Same WebGL2 baseline; WebGPU results reported separately, never substituted
measures: Target-frame coherence judged blind from paired screenshots
Time and code required to adjust light, material, fog, shadow and color grade
Cold-load transfer size and first meaningful rendered frame
Median and 1% low frame time during a fixed camera path
Draw calls, texture memory and shader compilation stalls
Whether interaction thresholds and evidence cues remain readable
decisionDrivingVisualBakeoff.passRule: Lock the route that reaches the approved target-frame intent within budget and without compromising evidence legibility; if results tie, choose the more reversible Three/R3F route.
decisionDrivingVisualBakeoff.blocker: The current session has no connected browser, so comparable screenshots and runtime frame evidence cannot yet be produced through the required browser-control surface.

runtimeVisualContractAfterLock.progressiveEnhancement: WebGPU may improve effects on supported browsers but cannot contain unique required gameplay cues.
runtimeVisualContractAfterLock.authoring: Blender to glTF 2.0; textures with explicit color-space roles; stable asset IDs; no direct remote-Wiki asset copying.
qualityBudgetsToSetBeforeFormalAssets: Initial scene and total downloadable asset transfer
Draw calls and visible triangle count
Median and 1% low frame time on the named reference device
Shader compilation and first meaningful frame
